parsed.study_design: Mixed-methods cross-sectional household survey with quantitative chi-square analysis and thematic coding of open-ended responses
parsed.population_and_sample: Residents of greater Tucson; 253 valid responses from a systematic random sample of 2,400 households mailed an English-language questionnaire
parsed.exposure: Trust in water-governance institutions and information sources, including utilities, wastewater facilities, regulators, elected officials, academics, and consultants
parsed.outcome: Self-reported willingness to drink reclaimed water if it matched or exceeded current tap-water quality, plus attitudes toward reclaimed-water uses
parsed.rationale: The Research Methods section (pp. 358–359) identifies the dependent variable as hypothetical willingness to drink reclaimed water and tests its association with institutional trust. Although the study empirically examines governance factors surrounding a potential municipal supply, the Findings (pp. 359–362) report public acceptance and risk perceptions rather than an outcome measuring actual access, connection, service availability, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion; therefore the outcome is outside the protocol’s eligible access outcomes.
